fields.h1: Build a Payroll Change Form That Gets Each Change Approved
fields.hero_description: Build a payroll change form that shows old and new pay side by side and sends each change to the right approvers.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Does With Each Pay Change
fields.features_subheading: A payroll change form records what changes in an employee's pay, the date it starts, and who approved it.
fields.feature_1:
Fields that follow the change type

Pick the kind of change at the top, and the form shows only the fields it needs. A transfer asks for the new department and manager; a stipend asks for the amount and the end date.
fields.feature_2:
Current and new values side by side

The app fills in the employee's current rate and department from your records. Approvers see the old value next to the new one, plus the difference, before they sign off.
fields.feature_3:
Approvers picked by change type

A rate change goes to the department head, then HR. A funding change goes to each account owner. Every approver gets an email or Slack alert, and the record logs who approved it.
fields.feature_4:
One queue for each pay period

Approved changes land in a list grouped by the pay period they start in. Payroll marks each one entered after keying it into the payroll system, and the date is saved on it.
fields.feature_5:
Approved changes sent by API

If your payroll provider offers an API, the app can send each change to it once the last approver signs off. If not, payroll works from the queue and keys each change in.
fields.feature_6:
Every change on file, code included

Every change and its approval history stay in a database you own, filed by employee. Export the app's full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans whenever you want it.

fields.usecase_heading: Pay Changes Across Four Kinds of Employer
fields.tab_content_1:
A pay period's first Monday or no start date

Seraphina Quarshie promotes line cook Cosimo Szczepanski to shift lead at Fennimore Kitchens, from $17.50 to $19.25 an hour. The date picker offers only the Mondays that start a pay period: Nov 2, Nov 16, and Nov 30. She picks Nov 2, and payroll coordinator Florian Dalgaard gets an email with the change.
fields.tab_content_2:
$400 for each of 6 pay periods, then a reminder

Tamsin Ridge School District pays teacher Nyambura Abiodun a $2,400 stipend to coach girls' soccer. Once the principal approves it, she gets $400 in each of 6 pay periods. On Friday, Nov 13, the last day of the season, the app emails payroll clerk Evander Vukovic to end the stipend.
fields.tab_content_3:
Splits that reach 40 hours or stay in the form

Greywell University funds research technician Isidore Kemppainen from two grants. His department administrator puts 24 hours on Grant 4471 and 16 on Grant 5208, and the form will not submit until all 40 of his weekly hours are assigned. Dr. Tiernan Pimentel, who runs Grant 5208, then approves its 16 hours.
fields.tab_content_4:
Hours cut under 32 wait for a benefits check

Lucasta Family Clinic moves medical assistant Mirelle Lindgren-Moss from 40 to 24 hours a week from Monday, Nov 16. Benefits at the clinic start at 32 hours, so any change under 32 goes to HR lead Solveig Rask for a benefits review. The 3 other changes that period are marked ready for payroll.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Payroll Change Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps turn the payroll change form you use today into one that routes each change for approval, built with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Sort the changes you already process
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Name the approvers for each type
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull the last six months of pay changes and group them by type, such as rate changes and transfers. Each type becomes one choice at the top of the form, with its own set of questions underneath.
fields.howto_step_2_des: For every change type, list the approvers in order and what each one checks. A rate change might need the department head and then HR, while a transfer needs the manager on both sides. Note a backup for anyone who travels.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write down how often you pay and the date each pay period starts for the rest of the year. Give the form that calendar. Managers can then pick only an effective date that opens a period, never one that lands midway through.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write one prompt that names the change types, their fields, the approvers for each type, and your pay calendar. Emergent builds the form and its approval steps, with a database that stores every change. Adjust any of it by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Check whether your payroll system accepts changes through an API. If it does, have the app send each change after the last approval. If it does not, ask for a queue grouped by pay period that payroll works through and marks entered.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit a raise for one test employee and a transfer for another. Check that each one shows the right fields, reaches its approvers in order, and lands in the right pay period. Fix anything that misroutes before real data goes in.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish it and send managers the link
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the form and share the link with every manager who requests pay changes. Put it on your own domain (built into Emergent, uses credits) if managers already know your HR site, and retire the old PDF so every request comes through one place.

faq_plan.q: What is a payroll change form?
faq_plan.a: A payroll change form is the record an employer keeps when an employee's pay changes, such as a raise or a cut in weekly hours. It lists the current and new figures with the date the change takes effect, and each approver signs off on it.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a payroll change form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in one prompt: what kinds of change you handle, what each one asks for, who signs off, and when your pay periods start. Emergent builds the form with its routing and a database of every change. Run a few fake changes through it before managers get the link.

faq_plan.q: Can I turn my paper payroll change form template into an online form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. List the boxes on your current template in a prompt, from the employee ID and the old and new rate down to the signature lines. Emergent builds an online version with the same fields. If what you have today is a payroll change form PDF, keep its section order so managers recognize it on first use.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a free payroll change form for a small business?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing the form. Keep bank account updates off it and on a separate direct deposit form, which keeps account numbers out of the records that hold rate changes.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a payroll change form include?
faq_plan.a: Start with the employee's name and ID, the change type, the current value, the new value, the effective date, and the reason. Then add the requester, each approver with the date they signed off, and an employee acknowledgment if your policy asks for one. The app can capture that acknowledgment as an e-signature.

faq_plan.q: When should a payroll change form be submitted?
faq_plan.a: Before the payroll cutoff for the pay period the change starts in. Set your own deadline ahead of that cutoff, such as 3 business days, to give approvers time to act. Have the app remind any approver who still has an open change 2 days before your deadline.

faq_plan.q: Can a payroll change form handle a change in hours or schedule?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the change affects pay: new weekly hours, a move between full-time and part-time, or a shift that carries a different rate. If the new schedule comes out of an employee's request for an accommodation, keep that request on a reasonable accommodation request form and file only the resulting pay change here.

faq_plan.q: Who should approve a payroll change form?
faq_plan.a: Set approvers by change type instead of one list for everything. For example: the employee's manager on every change, the department head on rate changes, HR on status changes, and the owner of each budget or grant account on funding changes. Have payroll enter a change only after its last approval.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep payroll change forms secure?
faq_plan.a: Collect only what each change needs, keep bank details on their own form, and limit who can open the records to HR and payroll. The records live in a database you own, on a platform with SOC 2 Type I and ISO 27001, instead of in a shared inbox or spreadsheet.

faq_plan.q: How do I track a payroll change form that is still waiting for approval?
faq_plan.a: Filter the app's list of changes by status. Each payroll change form is one record that shows who has approved it and who has not yet. It is the same setup you would give a refund request form: one record per request, with a named approver and a status anyone with access can check.

plan.angle: The top 10 is fixed paper and PDF forms (a county, a school service center, a university research office, a 3-part carbonless form, an HR association's status change form) plus two form-builder templates. Each one is a list of boxes: old value, new value, effective date, reason, signature lines. This page is for the HR or payroll lead building their own: the form changes its fields by change type, shows the current and new values side by side, ties effective dates to the pay calendar, routes each change type to its own approvers, and lands every approved change in one queue payroll works from, in a database the employer owns.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Payroll Change Form That Gets Each Change Approved'; hero 'shows old and new pay side by side and sends each change to the right approvers' covers the form's whole job.

intent.evidence: Builder-fit SERP (Jotform, workforce.com templates): page gives the fields ('Start with the employee's name and ID, the change type, the current value, the new value, the effective date, and the reason'), routing, template-to-online FAQ and a 7-step how-to.

specificity.evidence: Payroll vocabulary: 'pay period', 'payroll cutoff', 'Grant 4471', 'stipend', 'keying it into the payroll system'.

openers.evidence: Bodies open on full sentences: 'Pick the kind of change at the top...', 'Seraphina Quarshie promotes line cook Cosimo Szczepanski...'.

craft.evidence: QC clean; one ', so' ending (tab 4) under the limit; numbers stated plainly: $2,400 = 6 x $400, 24 + 16 = 40.

voice.evidence: Calm and concrete: 'Payroll marks each one entered after keying it into the payroll system, and the date is saved on it.' One wording note recorded.

truth.evidence: Emergent sentences map to prompt-build, alerts, api-connect ('If your payroll provider offers an API'), database-owned, code-export, free-start, soc2-iso, e-signature-capture, custom-domain. No tax, wage-law or payroll-compliance claims; the 32-hour benefits line is the clinic's own policy. Nov 2/16/30 and Nov 16 are Mondays and Nov 13 a Friday in 2026. FAQ 1 PA7 flag goes to Divit's packet, not a finding.

distinct.evidence: Not a copy of payroll-automation (timesheets, overtime, cutoff reminders, provider sync): this page is the change request itself, with change-type fields, pay-period dates, funding splits and stipend end dates.

faq.evidence: 10 builder-intent questions answered first; hub link in item 2; links direct deposit form, reasonable accommodation request form, refund request form; secondaries template, pdf, free, forms worked in; paa --spec 9 pass, 0 reject, 1 flag (PA7 on Q1, for Divit).
